A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-parroting work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting evaluations on 135 chaotic systems and four additional SciML datasets, together with noise, sampling-rate, embedding-dimension, and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original forecasting evaluations and adds comparator results, long-rollout invariant-property measurements, and power-spectrum analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 is identical: match the final length-D motif using Euclidean distance, exclude nearby motifs, and repeat the continuation following the closest match. The mathematical formulations are retained. Different experimental choices of D do not change the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 135-system dysts benchmark and the same vortex-flow, ECG, electronic-circuit, and Kuramoto data. 'Turbulence' and 'Circuit' rename existing table rows. Longer rollouts and the 129-system spectral-analysis subset change evaluation settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Moirai-2.0 and DynaMix to the main comparisons, including Figure 2 and Tables 1–3. Appendix B also evaluates simplex projection and AutoARIMA in Figures 7–8. v2 compared against Chronos, Chronos Bolt, TimesFM, and TimeMoE; simplex projection was discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The standard 300-step benchmark pipeline remains, but v3 adds 9,488- and 10,000-step rollout protocols, spectral Hellinger distance, and Lyapunov-exponent evaluation. Figure 4 changes the reported embedding dimension from 10 to 5 and extends the plotted context range from 32,768 to 65,536. These are substantial evaluation additions and revisions.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 and Appendix D investigate whether periodic parroted forecasts preserve spectra and dynamical invariants over long rollouts. Figure 12 adds spectral sensitivity to context length. Conversely, v2's cross-model VPT-versus-context analysis is removed. The noise and sampling-rate analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 Table 1 identifies its existing uncertainty values as standard deviations. New Table 4 reports standard deviations and correlation bounds described as p-value-based; Figure 12 specifies standard-deviation bands. The corresponding scaling analysis loses v2 Figure 11's bootstrap standard error and regression uncertainty band. Retained experiments still state 20 or 100 initial conditions.

E6.justification: v3 adds comparator and long-rollout results and revises several Parrot error and VPT curves. The scaling-dimension correlation changes from 0.51±0.08 in v2 Figure 11 to approximately 0.85 in v3 Section 5.2. These revisions are not fully explained as comparable-setting gains. Existing-method scores in Tables 1–3 and the noise/sampling tables are retained, while added competitors change some rankings.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 corrects the geometric scaling argument to concern a point's nearest neighbor, replacing v2's statement about distances between two random points. v3 also introduces an explicit attention-versus-nearest-neighbor complexity comparison. The scaling relation, kernel formulations, and appendix propositions and proofs remain; relocating the mathematical overview introduces no new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions remain substantially the same. The introduction broadens the superiority claim to the expanded comparator set, including classical methods. The conclusion adds the stronger interpretation that a foundation model unable to beat parroting has arguably failed to learn the underlying physics.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes periodic forecasts' asymptotic Lyapunov behavior from finite-time estimates and attributes DynaMix's long-term geometric fidelity to its recurrent architecture. It qualifies transformer-specific context limits, expands stationarity and stochastic-system limitations, and proposes parameter-inference and unseen-bifurcation tests beyond reconstruction. These substantially develop the paper's mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 adds a reproducibility statement pointing to a Python implementation and benchmarks, plus technical specifications for added models and spectral-estimation procedures. It removes v2's CPU-only timing description and explicit VPT definition and threshold despite retaining VPT results. The PDFs establish the new code-access statement, not the external resource's availability.

R1.justification: v3 extends discussion and citations to DynaMix, Moirai-2.0, Chronos-2, recurrent forecasting, language correlation dimension, and generalization beyond observed state space. It adds invariant-estimation references and replaces Huke's embedding guide with Takens. The existing related-work framework and central research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes focused rewrites in Methods, Results, and Conclusion, moves the mathematical overview from Section 3 to Appendix F.1, and adds a reproducibility section. Headings and citation style change throughout. Much of the prose and the main section sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the runtime figure with multipanel spectral forecasts, redesigns Figure 5, and relocates the aggregate scaling display to Appendix Figure 10. It expands comparison plots and tables, splits Figure 8, adds long-rollout Table 4 and Figures 11–12, and removes v2's VPT-context figure. The document template and ranking highlights also change.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important weaknesses in v2's evidence by evaluating a specialist dynamics model and classical forecasting baselines, and by directly testing invariant preservation far beyond the original 300-step forecasts. The finite-time versus periodic-behavior discussion also clarifies a central limitation. Removing the runtime plot, VPT definition, and scaling bootstrap uncertainty reduces transparency, and several revised results remain insufficiently explained. Nevertheless, the more demanding comparisons and long-rollout analyses substantially strengthen the paper's empirical foundation.
